name: MEWBURN
summary: Parsed Sustainable Procurement Policy template from Sustainable Procurement Policy.docx.

declaration.declaration: The objective of this Sustainable Procurement Policy is to ensure that Mewburn Ellis LLP integrates environmental, labour and human rights issues into all procurement processes. By doing so, we aim to promote sustainability, reduce our environmental footprint, and support ethical and responsible sourcing practices, fostering long-term partnerships with suppliers and business partners who share our commitment to sustainability.
declaration.scope: This policy applies to all operating sites where Mewburn Ellis conducts its business activities, covering all employees (whether permanent, fixed term or temporary), contractors, stakeholders.

General Procurement Sustainability Targe: Ensure all suppliers acknowledge and adhere to the Supplier Code of Conduct.
Environmental issues: Environmental Certification: We prefer to use suppliers that have environmental policies and with recognised environmental certifications (e.g., ISO 14001, EcoVadis, CDP etc.) to ensure compliance with environmental standards.
Energy Efficiency: We favor suppliers that use energy-efficient technologies and renewable energy sources in their operations.
Local Sourcing: We encourage procurement from local suppliers to reduce transportation emissions and support local economies.
To ensure that all procured products comply with environmental regulations and standards, we ask that all suppliers acknowledge that they have read and understand our supplier code of conduct.
We aim to train our procurement staff on environmental issues associated with purchasing decisions to promote sustainable and responsible sourcing practices.
To prioritize sourcing materials and services from suppliers committed to sustainable practices and environmental stewardship, we have trained our purchasers on this.
Labor and Human Right Issues: Ensure that suppliers understand we expect them to adhere to fair labour standards and provide safe working conditions for employees, including fair wages, reasonable working hours, and access to healthcare and other benefits as part of our supplier code of conduct.
We prefer to work with suppliers that uphold strong labour and human rights policies and possess recognized certifications (e.g., SA8000, ISO 45001) to ensure ethical and responsible practices.

We ask that all suppliers acknowledge that they have read and understood our supplier code of conduct to ensure they provide safe working conditions and fair wages for employees. Supplier confirmation that they have read and understood our terms is reviewed annually.

Promote diversity by including minority-owned and women-owned businesses in the supply chain. Actively seek out diverse suppliers and provide them with opportunities to participate in procurement processes.
Require suppliers to uphold ethical standards and comply with relevant regulations as outlined in our supplier code of conduct.
We aim to train our procurement staff on labour and human rights issues related to sourcing to ensure ethical and socially responsible procurement practices.

targets.target: We aim for at least 100% of new suppliers to acknowledge and adhere to our Supplier Code of Conduct by FY 2024–5, using FY 2021–22 as the baseline year and have achieved this aim – now all new suppliers must do this.
Ensure that 100% of purchasers in the firm have received training on environmental and social issues associated during procurement by FY 2026-27 from a baseline of 2021/22.
Ensure that 10% of our existing suppliers have responded to our Sustainability survey by FY 2022-23 from a baseline of 2021/22.
Ensure that 100% of all new suppliers have completed our survey and acknowledged that they have read and understood our supplier environmental policy by FY 2026/27 from a baseline of 2021/22.

Ensure that 100% of all new suppliers have completed our survey and acknowledged that they have read and understood our supplier diversity policy covering labour and human rights by FY 2026/27 from a baseline of 2021/22.

responsibilities.duty: Chief Commercial Officer is responsible for implementing this policy and ensuring all Partners and employees are aware of and adhere to this Policy.
All employees are responsible for familiarizing themselves with this Sustainable Procurement Policy and adhering to its principles in their procurement activities.
Employees are encouraged to report any concerns regarding supplier practices that may contradict this policy to their immediate supervisors or the designated compliance officer.
Regular monitoring and auditing of procurement processes to ensure compliance with sustainable procurement standards and practices.
Provide necessary training and resources to employees involved in procurement to enhance their understanding and implementation of sustainable procurement practices.
The CCO is responsible for implementation and overall oversight of this Sustainable Procurement Policy, including periodic review and updates as necessary.
Ensure that all procurement activities align with the principles and targets set forth in this policy.

Report on the effectiveness and compliance of this policy to senior management and stakeholders on a regular basis. Facilitate communication regarding sustainable procurement initiatives within the organization.

policy.monitoring:
Compliance and Performance Monitoring: We conduct annual audits to assess supplier compliance with reviewing and acknowledging environmental, labor, and ethical standards. Key metrics track the percentage of suppliers meeting environmental certifications and fair labor practices.

Supplier Engagement and Vetting: Annual reports track progress in including minority- and women-owned businesses in our supply chain.

Environmental Impact and Sustainability: We annually report on reducing our carbon footprint and promoting sustainable practices like local sourcing and waste reduction.

Ethical Standards and Corporate Governance: Annual reviews of our Sustainable Procurement Policy by the Chief Compliance Officer ensure alignment with corporate governance standards.

Mewburn Ellis LLP is committed to continuous improvement in our Sustainable Procurement practices. We regularly review and update our supplier engagement strategies to enhance diversity and sustainability metrics within our supply chain. Through our survey and code of conduct, we strive to ensure that all suppliers meet and exceed environmental, labor, and ethical standards set out in this policy. Our commitment to transparency includes regular reporting on our progress towards achieving targets related to environmental impact. By integrating feedback and lessons learned into our procurement processes, we aim to uphold the highest standards of sustainability and ethical conduct while driving positive social and environmental outcomes.
policy.reviewMechanism: The Chief Commercial Officer at Mewburn Ellis LLP will review the Sustainable Procurement Policy annually, and any updates will be communicated as necessary.
